narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Five sixths is the smallest, because six is the smallest number at the bottom.
<bookmark mark='pieces'/>A sixth is a longer piece than a twelfth, not a shorter one.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The bottom number alone cannot set the order. All three need one unit first.
removed_beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble points at the second set and says five sixths is the smallest because 6 is the smallest bottom number; one sixth and one twelfth of the same string are laid side by side; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check your order, write all three fractions in the common unit again.
<bookmark mark='up'/>The top numbers should go up from left to right, with none out of place.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor; the recap board shows both orders and the check: in the common unit, the tops go up from left to right

old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu says five sixths is the smallest because six is the smallest bottom number. Sixths are the biggest pieces in that set, so the bubble is struck.
